# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural issue with his heart that the doctors have been monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion, which makes meal times very stressful, and he's extremely picky and refuses many foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets exhausted very quickly when playing outside or running around, and he has speech difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks people to repeat what they've said because he didn't catch it the first time, indicating potential hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things that are far away, like the board in his classroom.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem to break or chip really easily, even with proper care.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and some have large front teeth or other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing difficulties may affect his learning, and he may require extra support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech difficulties and may have behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers or other skeletal anomalies.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and prevent further breakage or chipping.
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor the patient's hearing and address any potential hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor the patient's vision and address any potential vision problems.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart condition and address any potential concerns.
* Speech therapy to address the patient's speech difficulties.
* Behavioral therapy to address any potential behavioral differences.
* Occupational therapy to support the patient's development and address any potential delays.
* Physiotherapy to support the patient's physical development and address any potential delays.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets very tired after little physical activity and has delayed speech development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with fluid in the ear, which may be affecting his hearing, and has speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and some have speech delay.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus, indicating potential eyesight issues.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with chewing harder foods, suggesting potential issues with tooth strength or texture.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech development is delayed.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty keeping up with other kids during play, gets winded quickly, and needs to take breaks, suggesting potential heart-related issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has slower weight gain compared to her peers, despite being provided with nutritious meals and snacks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is not as graceful as her peers, often tripping over her own feet or dropping things, suggesting potential neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets overwhelmed in loud environments, covering her ears, and has difficulty with hearing, suggesting potential issues with her ears.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus, and her eyes seem to get tired easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, particularly with cold foods and drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups crucial.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, with some attending mainstream primary school and others requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often exhibit behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with scoliosis and hip dysplasia, which are being managed and treated by her doctors.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to assess for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to evaluate for vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to investigate potential heart conditions
* Skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for skeletal anomalies
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and behavioral differences
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient breathes faster than expected when playing actively, indicating possible cardiac concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is fussy about eating certain foods due to their texture, indicating potential gastrointestinal issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets exhausted easily when engaging in active play, suggesting potential neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing when the TV volume is at a normal level, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism and needs glasses to correct her vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs more frequent dental check-ups than most kids her age to ensure her teeth stay healthy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have weak enamel, large front teeth, and other dental concerns, requiring regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a noticeably different posture when standing or walking.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to increased curvature of the spine, and may experience skeletal anomalies, such as short fingers or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to detect any potential hearing issues
* Eyesight review to monitor vision and correct any issues
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess heart health
* Consideration of a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor bone health
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and address any concerns.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a potential tethered cord issue that could affect her back and legs, and is waiting for more tests to understand it better.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have other neurological issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties and needs the TV volume to be turned up high, indicating potential conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects her ability to see distant objects clearly and is impacting her schoolwork.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, even when eating soft foods, which is concerning for her smile and oral health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's hypermetropia and hearing difficulties are affecting her schoolwork, particularly when watching the board or following instructions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems developmentally behind other kids her age, and has speech difficulties that make it hard to understand what she's saying.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Consideration of behavioral therapy to address any behavioral differences or developmental delays

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that is monitored regularly with check-ups, which hasn't caused any big issues so far.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had feeding difficulties as a baby, with trouble latching on properly and getting frustrated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with a tethered cord, which hasn't seemed to affect her development too much.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of children with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had otitis media when she was younger, but it's been treated and she hears just fine now.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which is corrected with glasses.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth can break or chip pretty easily, so she needs to watch what she eats and brush them regularly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel and other dental concerns, and regular dental check-ups are recommended.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis and hip dysplasia, which are being monitored and managed with physical therapy and regular orthopedic check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of the spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent breakage or chipping
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor for any changes in hearing
* Regular eyesight reviews to monitor for any changes in vision
* Regular check-ups to monitor the septal defect and adjust treatment as needed
* Physical therapy and regular orthopedic check-ups to manage scoliosis and hip dysplasia
* Monitoring of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect in her heart, and further tests are pending to determine the course of action.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient can be quite picky about food, making mealtime stressful, but aside from that, her digestion seems okay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has seizures, which started a few months ago, and the family is still trying to find the right medication to control them.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has concerns with her hearing, as she sometimes doesn't respond immediately when called, and there have been instances where she seems not to hear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision, squints when reading or watching TV, and has concerns about her eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth compared to the rest of her teeth, which could potentially affect her self-esteem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large permanent upper middle teeth (macrodontia of upper central incisors) and may experience other dental concerns such as weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) due to learning difficulties.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, and the degree of delay ranges from mild to severe. They may also have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has short fingers on both hands and an unusual posture, which can make some tasks harder for her.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), short fingers (brachydactyly), and curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's dental health, especially given her large front teeth and potential for weak enamel.
* Regular hearing reviews to assess and address any hearing concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct any vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor the patient's heart condition.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with consideration for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support the patient's development and address any delays or difficulties.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences irregular bowel movements, which can be managed with dietary adjustments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord issue affecting her spinal development, which is being closely monitored by specialists.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media in the past, causing discomfort and pain, and may have conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to sit close to the television and holds books near her face, indicating possible vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, particularly to cold temperatures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have weak enamel, large front teeth, and other dental concerns, requiring regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

* Monitoring of growth velocity, with potential referral for endocrine investigations if growth is significantly below expected levels.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue in her heart that is monitored regularly through check-ups with her cardiologist. 
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion to certain textures and tastes, which can make mealtime challenging. She also has difficulty chewing harder foods like meats or raw vegetables.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hypotonia, which affects her muscle tone. Physical therapy has been helpful in managing this condition and improving her overall mobility. She also has a speech delay and struggles with communication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets overwhelmed in loud environments and can become easily frustrated. She also has astigmatism, which requires her to wear glasses to correct her vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which requires her to wear glasses to correct her vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing harder foods like meats or raw vegetables and has to adapt her diet to include softer options.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with communication and has a speech delay, which her speech therapist is working to address.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with communication and has a speech delay. She also has a feeding aversion to certain textures and tastes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental health and address any concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor vision and address any concerns.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health.

* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address developmental delays and communication challenges.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Regular monitoring of the patient's valve issue in her heart through check-ups with her cardiologist.

* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structurally abnormal heart that requires regular monitoring and tracking to ensure it develops and functions properly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery and others needing monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences irregular bowel movements, which can cause discomfort but are not too serious.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy, which is managed as a challenge by the family.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fluid in his ear, affecting his hearing, and is being monitored and followed up with a specialist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia and is in the process of getting glasses to correct it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has larger than usual front teeth, emphasizing the importance of regular dental care to prevent further issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Besides large front teeth, people with KBG syndrome may experience weak enamel, requiring careful brushing and regular dental check-ups, especially with a specialist SEN dentist for those with significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient developmentally takes a bit longer to catch up with his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but possibly requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans in secondary school due to the extra demands.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with speech clarity and expressing himself clearly at times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of spinal bones leading to scoliosis, delayed closure of the soft spot on the head, short fingers with curvature, and hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and prevent dental issues.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially in the first few years, to address conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to correct vision problems such as myopia.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis to monitor heart conditions.
* Consideration of a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to identify any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and manage challenges.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with a septal defect, which means there's a hole in the wall between the chambers of her heart. She works closely with her cardiologist to manage this condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: Mealtime can be challenging. Sometimes she has trouble eating certain foods or digesting them properly, which leads to discomfort and other issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: She experiences seizures. They can be scary, but she's learned how to handle them and works with her neurologist to control them as much as possible.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported as having seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: Loud noises seem to really bother her. She gets frustrated in noisy places, like malls or playgrounds, and sometimes covers her ears to block out the sound.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: She often rubs her eyes, especially when she's trying to focus on something. It's like she's having trouble seeing clearly or getting distracted easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: She's had to take her to the dentist pretty regularly. She's had some issues that needed attention, and the dentist has been keeping an eye on her teeth to prevent more problems.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

a) How this affects the patient: She also has scoliosis, which affects her spine and requires regular monitoring and treatment to prevent further complications.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine. Babies may experience a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and prevent dental issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to detect any hearing problems.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart condition.
* Skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor skeletal development.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and manage symptoms.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
